page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. No margin notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Catchword at bottom right below the last line.

main_text.p: autem, nondum concessisse tum facis, constare potest, quod triennio ante eversas Hierosolymas, Neronis anno XIIII[?] demùm è medio sublatus. Quanquam Scaliger, cum quibusdam recentioribus, conjiciat in ipsissimum annum perfectionis primæ, qui Neronis fuit nonus, vel decimus, Christi LXIII[?], vel LXIV. Indè verò à Pauli excessu, res Judæorum labascere, in peius ruere, turbari, miscerique summis, imminensque exitium genti prænunciari.

IV. Excipit notatum aliis argumentum, ex parte methodi & ordinis, in Epistola observati. Duabus siquidem partibus absolvitur, altera διδασκαλικὴ[?], sive doctrinalis & theoretica; altera παρακλητικὴ[?], sive moralis & practica. Prior, doctrinalis de Christi Persona, capitibus I, II, III, IV; de Christi sacerdotali Officio, & Beneficiis, capitibus V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, ex parte etiam X; de Fide & percipiendi modo, capitibus X, XI. Posterior, hortatoria ad Christianas virtutes, tolerantiam, constantiam in adversis, sanctimoniam, pacem, charitatem, [illegible, ~10 letters]

page.notes: The Greek words in the second paragraph are only partly legible; the two Greek adjectives after "altera" are marked [?] and are reproduced as best read. The Greek word after "altera" in the Posterior sentence and the words in the final line are blurred. The last line of the page is cut off at the right edge and reads "charitatem," followed by a word that is not legible; it is marked illegible. The Roman numerals "XIIII" and "LXIII" are uncertain (the print is smudged) and are marked [?]. The small mark at the bottom right corner below the catchword and the stray marks at the page edges are not printed text and are left out. The running head reads "ad Hebræos" with the "ad" in bold-looking type; the final letters are uncertain. The catchword is unclear and marked [?].
